title: Staggered On‑call Patterns and Status Concierge Playbook
author: Aisha Menon
body:
Summary:

This document describes a staggered on‑call pattern used at Redwood Inference and a companion 'Status Concierge' protocol for customer‑facing updates. It standardizes: rotation models, handoff scripts, primary/secondary responsibilities, fast mitigation steps for our common incidents (latency spike, KV cache thrash, noisy-tenant GPU contention, model-quality regression), game‑day objectives, and customer/status‑page templates.

Goals:
- Reduce responder fatigue and maintain coverage across timezones through staggered shifts.
- Shorten time to acknowledge (TTA) target to <= 3 minutes for P1s during business hours, <= 10 minutes off-hours.
- Provide a single, vetted customer status narrative per incident (Status Concierge) to avoid conflicting comms.
- Keep post‑incident action items small, measurable, and owned.

Quick reference: SLOs and thresholds
- P1 (Service outage): customer‑facing errors > 5% of requests or 50% latency regression above SLO for > 5 min.
- P2 (Major degradation): 5–15% token increase in median latency, or single-region capacity saturation.
- P3 (Minor): transient errors < 5% or nonblocking performance dips.
- Ack targets: P1 <= 3m (business), <= 10m (off-hours). P2 <= 15m. P3 <= 24h.

1) Staggered rotation model (pattern overview)
- Core concept: Instead of 24h shifting single long oncall, we adopt staggered, overlapping shifts to improve continuity and handoff quality.
- Roles in each rotation week: Primary (8h focused window), Secondary (follow for 16h), Rota Steward (weekly owner who owns schedule, non‑pager).
- Shift blocks (example for NA/EU/APAC):
  1. Morning Focus (08:00–16:00 local primary) — business hours coverage and product support.
  2. Evening Bridge (16:00–00:00) — handoff to next region and high traffic exfil.
  3. Overnight Triage (00:00–08:00) — light coverage, escalation to oncall if P1.
- Overlap: adjacent shifts overlap by 1 hour for structured handoff.

2) Roster rules and rotation cadence
- Teams publish 3 months of schedule in advance to the rotation calendar.
- Each engineer signs up for at most 2 primary weeks per quarter.
- Primary receives a weekly oncall allowance (comp time or stipend) and must complete a post-shift checklist.
- Rota Steward validates coverage, ensures runbook links, and runs a 15m pre‑shift briefing if the week includes a planned deployment.

3) Handoff checklist (to be completed in the last 30 minutes of a shift)
- TL;DR status: current open incidents, SLOs in breach, maintenance windows active.
- Evidence: links to dashboards (latency, errors, capacity), last 30m logs, recent pagination/context.
- Active mitigation steps: list current mitigations, who is executing, expected ETA.
- Followups: postmortem owner (if unresolved), tasks for incoming primary.
- Confirm Slack channel bridge is healthy and the status page draft exists if incident active.

4) Incident process (short run loop)
1. Signal: automated monitor triggers (SLO alert) or external report.
2. Acknowledge: Primary follows triage checklist within ack target. Record ack timestamp.
3. Triage (5–15 min): identify scope (region, model, tenant), impact (customers, internal), and quick mitigations (scale, fallback, route).
4. Escalate: if P1 or multi-region, notify SRE lead, Eng PM, and Customer Success (CS) liaison.
5. Contain & stabilize: apply short-lived mitigations — e.g., reduce model seq_len, shift traffic to alternate region, disable heavy routing policies, drain noisy instance pool.
6. Status Concierge: prepare the single canonical customer/status update (see templates below).
7. Restore & confirm: run post‑fix validation and close incident when SLOs return to baseline for 15 minutes.
8. Postmortem: within 72 hours assign owner and draft; final writeup due within 14 days.

5) Triage playbook snippets (common incidents)
- Latency spike (KV cache miss storm):
  1. Identify affected model(s) and tenant(s) via trace tags.
  2. Check KV cache hit-rate metric and eviction rate.
  3. Apply emergency mitigation: temporarily increase cache shard memory, or toggle prefix caching off for affected tenants.
  4. If hardware hot spots: shift traffic to warm pool and mark node for postmortem.
- Noisy‑neighbor GPU contention:
  1. Pinpoint tenant(s) with burst activity (usage dashboard).
  2. Move offending jobs to best-effort pool or throttle throughput using rate-limit policy.
  3. If Dedicated capacity affected, engage Customer Success for contract sensitivity.
- Model quality regression (sudden hallucination or prompt failure):
  1. Detect via eval regression alerts or incoming CSR.
  2. Rollback to previous pinned model revision or enable earlier quantization/variance profile.
  3. Notify product and research teams and start a quality postmortem.

6) Escalation matrix (who to call)
- P1: Primary -> SRE Lead -> Head of Platform -> CEO (only for major multi-customer outages).
- P2: Primary -> Team Lead -> Product PM -> CS Liaison.
- P3: Primary -> Team Slack triage -> schedule follow up in normal cadence.
- Pager policy: only escalate to executives for > 3 hours unresolved major impact or regulatory customer impacted.

7) Status Concierge protocol (customer & status page comms)
- Purpose: ensure one authoritative narrative and cadence for customers and public status.
- Ownership: the Primary owns the first status update; CS Liaison approves and publishes after 1st technical validation.
- Cadence: initial update within 15 minutes for P1, then regular updates every 30 minutes until stabilization, then hourly until resolved.
- Content checklist for every update:
  - Impact summary (who and what is affected).
  - What we know (current hypotheses).
  - What we are doing (actions in progress).
  - ETA for next update.
  - Mitigations available for customers (workarounds).

Status page template (short):
- Title: [Investigating] Increased latency for inference in us-west-2
- Body: We are investigating increased inference latency affecting a subset of customers in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively mitigating by shifting traffic and tuning KV caches. We will provide an update by 14:35 UTC.

Customer email/SMS template (first contact):
- Subject: Redwood Inference — Investigating impact to inference latency in us-west-2
- Body: Hello — We’re contacting you because we’ve detected elevated latency for inference requests in us-west-2 which may affect your service. Our engineering team is actively investigating and applying mitigations. We will follow up within 30 minutes with next steps. If you see critical production impact for your business, please reply to this message or contact your CSM.

8) Game‑day plan and objectives
- Objective: validate the staggered roster and Status Concierge under controlled stress.
- Frequency: quarterly per team; one cross‑team full stack drill per year.
- Scenario examples: KV cache eviction storm, noisy tenant spike, multi-region failover, model rollback under traffic.
- Success criteria: ack time targets met, single status narrative published, restoration within target SLA, postmortem action items assigned within 72 hours.
- Post‑game rituals: 30m retro within 48 hours, prioritized action list added to sprint backlog, runbook updates applied within 7 days.

9) Postmortem guide (short format)
- Use the incident template in /postmortem-templates/structured-incident-2023.md. Required fields: summary, timeline, root cause(s), mitigations during incident, long‑term corrective actions, owner and ETA for each action, customer impact summary, and a risk reduction score.
- Fast‑close rule: if mitigation fully prevented customer impact and RCA is trivial, use an abbreviated postmortem and mark as "fast-closed" with at least one preventive task.

10) Automation and tooling recommendations
- Dashboards: maintain a one‑screen panel per service: token latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization per pool, queue length.
- Alerts: compose alerts with runbook links (use templated URL variables) and include initial triage checklist.
- Status page automation: keep drafts in a shared folder accessible to rota steward; allow programmatic publish via statuspage API with approval toggle.

11) Preservation of evidence and post incident compliance
- For incidents with regulatory/customer evidence needs: capture full timeline, request IDs, traces and attach to postmortem. Evidence retention: 90 days for routine incidents; 2 years for regulated-customer incidents.

12) Templates and snippets (copy/paste)
- Slack bridge opener: "Incident: [P1] {service} — primary @ {primary_name} — short summary — link to status page: {url}"
- Run command examples:
  - Check KV hits: curl -s https://monitoring/api/metrics?metric=kv_cache_hit_rate&service=inference | jq
  - Drain instance: ri-cli instance drain --id i-012345 --reason "noisy-tenant"

13) Ownership and upkeep
- Runbook custodian: team lead must review and signoff on runbook content quarterly.
- Schedule owner: Rota Steward for each team keeps calendar and enforces shift limits.
- Playbook review: Ops council conducts an annual review and updates thresholds based on evolving traffic patterns.

Appendix: Useful links
- Service dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/inference
- Status page admin: https://status.redwood.ai/admin
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template-structured-2023.json

Contact and feedback
For questions about this pattern or to request a roster exception, contact the Rota Steward (rota-steward@redwood.ai) or open an issue in the oncall‑ops repo.
